searchField.available_title: Your exact trademark is available for registration
searchField.default_description_word:
Did you know that before your trademark gets registered, it is examined by IP Australia? This is when IP Australia can object to your application. Objections can be on a number of grounds including because of prior similar trademarks.

Before you apply to register your trademark, it is a good idea to conduct a search of the IP Australia trademark database to see whether the trademark is available for registration.

Our online application process conducts an exact word trademark search of IP Australia's trademark database before you submit your application to us for filing. This reveals exact word trademarks only so to obtain a more comprehensive trademark search before you file, get in touch with us.

*Only words can be searched via our online platform. If you require a logo search, get in touch with us.

searchClasses.title: Add your goods and/or services
searchClasses.default_title: What are classes of goods and services?
searchClasses.default_description:
Trademarks must be registered for goods and/or services which are divided into "classes".

Registering your trademark provides protection for the goods and/or services you provide. Here you need to select the goods/services relevant to your trade mark. Your application can cover more than one "class". For example "computer software" is in class 9 whereas "computer services" are in class 42.

Please enter your goods or services in the search bar. For example, software, clothing, advertising, computer programming, business, financial, retail, management, machine, book, car, furniture.

You may choose as many goods/services as you like. You can select more than one items in each class if needed. Once you have selected all of your goods/services, they will be listed in the side bar for your review before moving on with the application.
searchClasses.warning_title: Tips to avoid IP Australia rejecting your application
searchClasses.warning_description:
To avoid IP Australia rejecting your application, make sure your trade mark does not describe your goods or services or any feature of your goods or services. For example, an application for “DOG” for pet accessories would be rejected by IP Australia.

If you are concerned your trade mark describes your goods or services, adding another element to your trademark, such as a word, logo, slogan or a combination of these may avoid rejection by IP Australia.
